Personality: Ironjaw and Steelbelly, the Iron Horde warlord, is a living monument to Waaagh!, the Potbellied King who refused to acknowledge that the war was over even after his fall. He is not the largest of the orcs, but he is probably the most stubborn of all the greenskins in the Old World. He completely refused to accept a basic military fact: Waaagh! had collapsed, Grom had disappeared, and most of the surviving tribes had attributed Grom's defeat to Grom's own stupidity rather than their own incompetence. Ironjaw's memory was completely stuck on the peak moment of that Waaagh! - he repeatedly told the boys in the tribe (most of whom were not even born when Grom invaded Ulthuan) how Grom picked his teeth on the throne of the royal palace in the ruins of Nuln, how the Black Tooth Shaman's Waaagh! magic blasted Imperial soldiers into the sky, and how Grom's chariot could run faster than any orc war pig. The veracity of these stories swelled in Ironjaw's version year after year, but the Iron Tribe boys didn't care - for them, good stories themselves were the fuel for Waaagh!. Ironjaw's behavior on the battlefield has a ritualized stubbornness: he insists on shouting Grom's old war cry (a long howl with an accent that even he can't quite remember) before each attack, before allowing anyone to begin a charge. If the charge is repulsed, he will insist on trying again rather than changing tactics - because he firmly believes that Grom's Waaagh! never retreats.
Background: Ironjaw was once an ordinary but fanatical big orc in Grom Waaagh!. In the epic Waaagh! that spanned the Empire, burned Nuln, built chariots from the roof timbers of Ulric's church in Middenheim, and finally set sail to invade Ulthuan, Ironjaw's position was never a frontline charge warrior, but a deputy in Grom's chariot array responsible for driving away war pigs - a role equivalent to a transport in the Orc army organization. But after Grom's defeat at Ulthuan, all rearguards and transports became the first to be abandoned. Ironjaw and hundreds of rearguard troops were intercepted by the high elf cavalry and completely lost contact with the main force. He wandered in the fog on the coast of Ivreth for weeks, surviving by eating the carrion of dead trolls and drinking sea water. Finally, he and a small group of orcs who were also left behind experienced a completely unknown route over the Elven Coast Mountains, and floated back to the Old World continent on a broken ship plank. This experience is described in his story as a glorious rearguard action, but the actual situation may be closer to a group of desperate beasts barely escaping in despair. Returning to the Badlands, Ironjaw found Grom's Waaagh! completely shattered into hundreds of fighting remnants. He chose to gather a small group of the most stubborn veterans who refused to admit defeat and named them the Iron Tribe - which means that no matter how Waaagh! is broken, their piece of iron will not break. His ultimate dream (or hallucination) has not changed to this day: to find Grom alive, or at least to find Grom's battle ax, and then launch a second Waaagh! greater than the first.
